glossary.full: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
glossary.text: The federal law that protects health information. Its Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules apply to hospitals and to the vendors that handle their data.
Health information that can be tied to a person and is held by a hospital, a health plan or their vendors. HIPAA limits how it is used and shared; ePHI is the electronic form.
An organization HIPAA applies to directly: a health care provider that bills electronically, a health plan or a clearinghouse. A hospital is a covered entity.
A vendor that creates, receives, keeps or sends protected health information for the hospital. It needs a signed agreement before it starts and must report breaches to the hospital.
The contract HIPAA requires with each business associate. It sets permitted uses, safeguards, breach reporting and what happens to the data at the end.
The document that tells patients how the hospital uses their health information and what rights they have. HIPAA sets its content, and it must be given, posted and on the website.
A patient's signed permission for a use or disclosure that HIPAA does not otherwise allow, such as marketing. The patient can revoke it in writing at any time.

glossary.full: Treatment, Payment and Health Care Operations
glossary.text: The three everyday purposes for which HIPAA lets a hospital use and share health information without a signed authorization.
The rule that only the health information needed for the purpose is used, shared or asked for. It does not apply to disclosures for treatment.
A patient's right to see and get a copy of their records. The limit is 30 days today and becomes 15 calendar days when the Privacy Rule changes issued in November 2026 take effect.

An impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured protected health information. It is presumed reportable unless a four-factor risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised.
The four-factor review HIPAA requires after an impermissible disclosure: what information, who got it, whether it was actually viewed, and how far the risk was reduced.
The accurate and thorough assessment of risks to electronic health information that the Security Rule requires. Federal enforcement cites a missing or partial one more often than any other gap.

glossary.full: Department of Health and Human Services
glossary.text: The federal department that issues and enforces the HIPAA rules. Breaches are reported to it.
The part of HHS that investigates HIPAA complaints and breaches and can impose penalties. Patients can complain to it directly.
The federal agency that pays hospitals under Medicare and sets the Conditions of Participation, the emergency care rules and the price transparency rules.
The federal standards a hospital must meet to be paid by Medicare and Medicaid. They cover patient rights, medical records, quality and emergency readiness, among others.

glossary.full: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
glossary.text: The federal law that requires a hospital emergency department to screen and stabilize anyone who comes for care, whatever their ability to pay.
The federal rule that gives extra protection to substance use disorder treatment records. It applies only to federally assisted programs and the records they share.
A practice that is likely to interfere with access to, exchange or use of electronic health information. Federal rules prohibit it unless a listed exception applies.
The published collection of federal agency rules. A reference such as 45 CFR 164.312 means title 45, part 164, section 312.
A requirement whose compliance date has not arrived yet. It is shown as readiness and kept out of the in-force score.
A voluntary federal framework that organizes security work into six functions: govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover.
Twenty voluntary goals HHS published for health care in 2024: ten essential and ten enhanced. They point at the practices that stop the most common attacks.
The body that publishes international standards. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 sets the requirements for an information security management system.
The policies, roles, risk process and controls an organization uses to manage information security in a planned way. ISO/IEC 27001 defines what it must contain.
The document that lists every Annex A control, says whether the hospital needs it and why, and records its implementation status. Each approved version is kept.

The list of 93 reference controls at the back of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, in four themes: organizational, people, physical and technological. Every one must be accounted for in the Statement of Applicability.
The person accountable for information security. In many hospitals the IT head holds this role.
Signing in with a second proof, such as a code from a phone app, as well as a password. Here it is called two-step sign-in.
Giving access according to a person's role rather than person by person. In this product a role sets what each module allows, narrowed further by hospital, department and audit assignment.
Signing in once through the organization's identity system instead of a separate password for each application.
The longest a system may be down after a failure before the harm is unacceptable. The requirements document sets an initial target of 4 hours for this product.
The most data, measured in time, that may be lost in a failure. The requirements document sets an initial target of 1 hour for this product.
A system that collects security logs from many sources and raises alerts. Incidents can be fed from it.
The systems that create user identities and control what each can reach. It supplies information for access reviews.
Reading the words in a scanned page or photograph so they can be searched. It is used on evidence documents.
The level of a risk before any controls are taken into account, scored as likelihood multiplied by impact on scales of 1 to 5.
The level of a risk that remains after controls. A low residual score does not accept the risk: acceptance needs approval by an authorized person.
The decision about what to do with a risk: modify it with controls, retain it, avoid it or share it. Treatment actions are tracked to completion.
The combined practice of directing an organization, managing what could go wrong, and proving that laws and standards are followed.
The action taken to fix a problem that was found and to stop it happening again. Closure needs implementation evidence and an effectiveness check by someone other than the owner or implementer.
A requirement that is not met. A major nonconformity is a failure that undermines the system or the requirement as a whole; a minor one is a lapse that does not.
Something the auditor noticed that is not a nonconformity today but could become one, or the record of what was found in a test.
The recorded result of comparing what the auditor saw with the audit criterion. A finding keeps the link to the test it came from.
The requirement an audit test is judged against, such as a section of the HIPAA rules or an ISO clause, in a specific framework version.
The auditor's record of a test: what was examined, the sample, the result and the reviewer. Only auditors assigned to the audit can see them.
A measure the hospital operates to meet a requirement or reduce a risk. One control can be mapped to several requirements across frameworks, so its evidence is collected once.
A document or record that shows a control operates. Uploading it proves nothing until a reviewer who did not submit it has accepted it.
Whether a requirement applies to a particular hospital. A not-applicable decision needs a written justification and approval, and can be reassessed when operations or the law change.
Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant.
A measure of how well something is working. Each one here shows its calculation rule on hover.
Software provided over the internet for a subscription rather than installed by each customer.
A consultant running assessments and audits for several hospitals from one account. Each consultant sees only the hospitals assigned to them.
One customer organization on a shared installation. Each tenant's data is kept apart from every other tenant's.
The system that holds patients' clinical records and through which most care is ordered and documented.
The messages a hospital system sends when a patient is admitted, moved or discharged. Other systems use them to stay in step.
The number a hospital gives each patient. Records in this product refer to people by reference numbers, not names.
A network through which hospitals and other providers share patient records electronically.
The system that holds employee records. It can supply joiner and leaver dates for access reviews.
The number CMS assigns to a hospital that takes part in Medicare. It identifies the hospital in federal records.
The largest accrediting body for United States hospitals. This product does not issue accreditation; the same controls and evidence can support a survey.
The system that manages laboratory orders, samples and results.
The system that stores and displays radiology images such as X-rays, CT and MRI scans.

glossary.full: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine
glossary.text: The standard format and protocol for medical images. Imaging machines use it to send studies to the PACS.
A family of standards for exchanging clinical and administrative data between health systems.
The modern HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web interfaces.
The finance and purchasing system of record. It can supply vendor and contract information.
A defined way for one system to exchange data with another.
The standard for sending email. Notifications can be emailed when a mail server is configured.
A standard for passing user account information between systems.
The standard used for single sign-on with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Okta.

steps.label: If / else
steps.help: Branch on a field of the triggering record.

steps.help: Create a task for a role or a person.

steps.help: Pause until each role approves in turn.

steps.help: Send an in-app notification, and email if configured.

steps.help: Critical notice and urgent task for a senior role.

steps.help: Create a finding, CAPA or any other record.

steps.help: Set a field on the triggering record.

steps.label: Call webhook
steps.help: Send the event to n8n, Zapier or any URL.

steps.help: Request a recommendation for human review.

agents.name: Document analysis
agents.does: Reads an evidence document, identifies the requirements it is relevant to, suggests control mappings and retrieves similar evidence already on file.

agents.name: Gap identification
agents.does: Looks across a hospital's applicable requirements for missing controls, missing or expired evidence, failed tests and recorded gaps.

agents.name: Audit observation drafting
agents.does: Drafts the wording of an audit observation from the criterion, the sample and the auditor's notes.

agents.name: Corrective action suggestions
agents.does: Suggests lines of enquiry for root cause and possible corrective actions for a finding, drawing on similar earlier actions.

agents.name: Audit report drafting
agents.does: Drafts the audit report from the audit's scope, criteria, test results and findings.

agents.name: Control mapping suggestions
agents.does: Suggests which existing controls address a requirement, for review mapping by mapping.

_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.description: Separate mission-critical assets into their own network zones so that a compromise is contained.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Detect and respond to relevant threats and tactics
requirement.description: Know the threats and attacker methods relevant to the organization and be able to detect them on endpoints.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Cybersecurity mitigation
requirement.description: Set priorities for fixing what testing finds, and fix it.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Cybersecurity testing
requirement.description: Use penetration tests and attack simulations to find weaknesses and the ways they could be used.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Third-party incident reporting
requirement.description: Have a way to learn of and respond to known incidents or breaches at vendors and service providers.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Third-party vulnerability disclosure
requirement.description: Have a way to discover and respond to threats and weaknesses found in vendor products and services.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Asset inventory
requirement.description: Identify known, unknown and unmanaged assets to detect and respond to new weaknesses faster.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Vendor and supplier cybersecurity requirements
requirement.description: Identify, assess and reduce risks from third-party products and services.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Separate user and privileged accounts
requirement.description: Keep administrator accounts separate from everyday user accounts.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Unique credentials
requirement.description: Use unique credentials so that anomalous activity can be detected and traced.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Basic incident planning and preparedness
requirement.description: Be ready to respond to, and recover from, a significant cybersecurity incident.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Revoke credentials for departing workforce members
requirement.description: Remove access promptly when staff, contractors and volunteers leave.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Strong encryption
requirement.description: Encrypt sensitive data to keep it confidential in storage and in transit.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Basic cybersecurity training
requirement.description: Make sure staff learn and practice secure behavior.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Multifactor authentication
requirement.description: Add a second factor to protect accounts, especially those reachable from the internet.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Email security
requirement.description: Reduce risk from email threats such as spoofing, phishing and fraud.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Mitigate known vulnerabilities
requirement.description: Reduce the chance that attackers exploit known weaknesses in systems reachable from the internet.

_labels.framework: FW-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
_labels.version: FV-0009 · HHS Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals (January 2024)

requirement.title: Make the file easy to find
requirement.description: The file is linked from the website footer and referenced in a text file at the site root so that it can be found automatically.

_labels.framework: FW-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements
_labels.version: FV-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements (45 CFR Part 180 (with 2026 changes))

requirement.title: Show prices for shoppable services in a consumer-friendly way
requirement.description: Standard charges for at least 300 shoppable services are displayed in plain language, or a price estimator tool is offered.

_labels.framework: FW-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements
_labels.version: FV-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements (45 CFR Part 180 (with 2026 changes))

requirement.title: Publish a machine-readable file of standard charges with the required data
requirement.description: One file per hospital lists standard charges for all items and services in the CMS template, updated at least once a year. From 2026 it includes actual allowed amount figures and an attestation naming a senior official.

_labels.framework: FW-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements
_labels.version: FV-0008 · Hospital price transparency requirements (45 CFR Part 180 (with 2026 changes))

requirement.title: Document the exception relied on when information is not shared
requirement.description: When a request is delayed, limited or refused, the exception that applies and how its conditions are met are recorded.

_labels.framework: FW-0007 · Information blocking rules
_labels.version: FV-0007 · Information blocking rules (45 CFR Part 171)

requirement.title: Do not interfere with access to, exchange or use of electronic health information
requirement.description: A provider must not knowingly engage in a practice that is likely to interfere with access, exchange or use of electronic health information, unless the law requires it or an exception applies.
requirement.evidence_expected: Release of information practices; portal settings; request denials with reasons

_labels.framework: FW-0007 · Information blocking rules
_labels.version: FV-0007 · Information blocking rules (45 CFR Part 171)

requirement.title: Post signs about the right to examination and treatment
requirement.description: Signs in the emergency department tell patients their rights under the Act and whether the hospital takes part in Medicaid.

_labels.framework: FW-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
_labels.version: FV-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (42 U.S.C. 1395dd; 42 CFR 489.20 and 489.24)

requirement.title: Keep a central log and an on-call physician list
requirement.description: A log records everyone who comes for emergency care and what happened, and a list shows the physicians on call.

_labels.framework: FW-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
_labels.version: FV-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (42 U.S.C. 1395dd; 42 CFR 489.20 and 489.24)

requirement.title: Transfer unstable patients only when the conditions for an appropriate transfer are met
requirement.description: A transfer needs a physician certification or patient request, an accepting facility, records sent and qualified transport.

_labels.framework: FW-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
_labels.version: FV-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (42 U.S.C. 1395dd; 42 CFR 489.20 and 489.24)

requirement.title: Stabilize an emergency medical condition
requirement.description: A patient with an emergency condition is treated until stable, or appropriately transferred.

_labels.framework: FW-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
_labels.version: FV-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (42 U.S.C. 1395dd; 42 CFR 489.20 and 489.24)

requirement.title: Give a medical screening examination to anyone who comes to the emergency department
requirement.description: Anyone who comes to the emergency department asking for care gets an appropriate screening examination, whatever their ability to pay.

_labels.framework: FW-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
_labels.version: FV-0006 · Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (42 U.S.C. 1395dd; 42 CFR 489.20 and 489.24)

requirement.title: Maintain an emergency preparedness program
requirement.description: An all-hazards risk assessment, plan, policies, communication plan, training and testing are kept current.

_labels.framework: FW-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected)
_labels.version: FV-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected) (42 CFR Part 482 (selected sections))

requirement.title: Run a quality assessment and performance improvement program
requirement.description: A hospital-wide, data-driven program tracks quality indicators and adverse events and acts on them.

_labels.framework: FW-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected)
_labels.version: FV-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected) (42 CFR Part 482 (selected sections))

requirement.title: Send electronic patient event notifications
requirement.description: A hospital with a capable electronic record system sends admission, discharge and transfer notifications to the patient's other providers.

_labels.framework: FW-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected)
_labels.version: FV-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected) (42 CFR Part 482 (selected sections))

requirement.title: Keep accurate, complete and confidential medical records
requirement.description: Records are accurately written, promptly completed, authenticated, retained for at least five years and protected from loss, alteration and unauthorized use.
requirement.evidence_expected: Record completion audits; retention schedule; access controls

_labels.framework: FW-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected)
_labels.version: FV-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected) (42 CFR Part 482 (selected sections))

requirement.title: Protect patient rights, including privacy, confidentiality of records and a grievance process
requirement.description: Patients are told their rights, have personal privacy and confidential clinical records, can see their records and can file a grievance that gets a written answer.
requirement.evidence_expected: Patient rights notice; grievance procedure and log

_labels.framework: FW-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected)
_labels.version: FV-0005 · Medicare Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (selected) (42 CFR Part 482 (selected sections))

requirement.title: Give patients the Part 2 notice of privacy practices
requirement.description: Patients are told about the confidentiality protections and their rights at admission.

_labels.framework: FW-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records
_labels.version: FV-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records (42 CFR Part 2 (2024 final rule))

requirement.title: Protect Part 2 records and report breaches
requirement.description: Formal policies protect paper and electronic Part 2 records, and breaches are notified in the same way as under HIPAA.
requirement.evidence_expected: Security policy for Part 2 records; breach procedure

_labels.framework: FW-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records
_labels.version: FV-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records (42 CFR Part 2 (2024 final rule))

requirement.title: Send the required notice with each disclosure made with consent
requirement.description: Each disclosure made with consent carries a copy of the consent or a clear explanation of its scope, and the statement about use in legal proceedings.

_labels.framework: FW-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records
_labels.version: FV-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records (42 CFR Part 2 (2024 final rule))

requirement.title: Get written consent with the required elements before disclosing Part 2 records
requirement.description: Records of a federally assisted substance use disorder program are disclosed only with the patient's written consent or under a listed exception. A single consent may cover future treatment, payment and operations.

_labels.framework: FW-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records
_labels.version: FV-0004 · Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records (42 CFR Part 2 (2024 final rule))

requirement.title: Be able to show that notifications were made or were not required
requirement.description: The hospital carries the burden of proof and keeps the documentation.
requirement.evidence_expected: Incident register with decisions, approvals and timestamps

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Require business associates to report breaches to the hospital
requirement.description: A business associate notifies the hospital of a breach without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of discovery.

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Notify HHS
requirement.description: For 500 or more people, HHS is notified at the same time as the individuals. Smaller breaches are logged and reported within 60 days after the end of the calendar year.
requirement.evidence_expected: HHS breach portal submissions; annual log

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Notify the media when more than 500 residents of a state are affected
requirement.description: Prominent media outlets serving the state or jurisdiction are notified within the same 60 days.

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Notify affected individuals within 60 days of discovery
requirement.description: Each affected person is notified in writing without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the breach is discovered, with the required content.

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Assess every impermissible use or disclosure to decide whether it is a breach
requirement.description: An impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured health information is presumed to be a breach unless a documented risk assessment of four factors shows a low probability that the information was compromised.
requirement.evidence_expected: Breach risk assessments covering the four factors

_labels.framework: FW-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
_labels.version: FV-0003 · HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)

requirement.title: Keep security policies and documentation for six years
requirement.description: Policies, procedures and required records are written, kept for six years, made available to those who implement them and reviewed periodically.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Include the required terms in business associate contracts
requirement.description: The contract requires the business associate to comply with the Security Rule, bind its subcontractors and report security incidents and breaches.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Guard health information sent over a network

_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Verify that a person or entity is who they claim to be
requirement.description: Procedures verify the identity of anyone seeking access to electronic health information.

_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Protect health information from improper alteration or destruction
requirement.description: Policies and mechanisms protect the integrity of electronic health information.

_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Record and examine activity in systems that hold health information
requirement.description: Hardware, software or procedures record and allow examination of activity in systems containing electronic health information.
requirement.evidence_expected: Audit log configuration for each clinical system

_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Allow access only to authorized people and programs
requirement.description: Each user has a unique identifier and there is an emergency access procedure. Automatic logoff and encryption are addressable.
requirement.evidence_expected: Unique user identifiers; emergency access procedure; encryption settings

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Control devices and media that hold health information
requirement.description: Receipt, movement, re-use and disposal of hardware and media are controlled, with disposal and media re-use procedures required.
requirement.evidence_expected: Media disposal records; device movement log

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Physically secure workstations
requirement.description: Workstations that reach health information are protected so that only authorized users can use them.
requirement.evidence_expected: Screen lock settings; placement of nursing station screens

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Define proper workstation use
requirement.description: Policies set the functions performed, how they are performed and the surroundings of workstations that can reach health information.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Limit physical access to systems and the places that house them
requirement.description: Physical access to information systems and facilities is limited to authorized people, with plans for contingency access and maintenance records.
requirement.evidence_expected: Server room and records room access logs

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Get satisfactory assurances from business associates
requirement.description: A business associate may handle electronic health information only under a written contract that gives satisfactory assurances.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Evaluate security periodically
requirement.description: A technical and non-technical evaluation is performed periodically and when operations or the environment change.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Keep a contingency plan: backup, disaster recovery and emergency operation
requirement.description: Retrievable exact copies of health information are kept, with plans to restore lost data and to keep critical processes running, and the plans are tested.
requirement.evidence_expected: Backup reports; restore tests; disaster recovery plan

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Identify, respond to and document security incidents
requirement.description: Suspected and known incidents are identified and responded to, harmful effects are reduced and outcomes are documented. Required.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Run a security awareness and training program
requirement.description: All workforce members, including management, receive security training, with reminders, malware protection, log-in monitoring and password management addressed.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Authorize access to health information by role
requirement.description: Policies govern who is granted access to which systems and how access is established and changed.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Make sure only authorized workforce members can reach health information
requirement.description: Access is authorized and supervised, cleared where appropriate, and removed when employment or the need ends.
requirement.evidence_expected: Joiner, mover and leaver records; access removal evidence

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Name a security official
requirement.description: One person is responsible for developing and implementing the security policies and procedures.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Review records of information system activity regularly
requirement.description: Audit logs, access reports and security incident reports are reviewed on a regular schedule. Required.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Apply sanctions for security policy violations
requirement.description: Workforce members who fail to follow security policies face appropriate sanctions. Required.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Manage the risks found to a reasonable and appropriate level
requirement.description: Security measures are put in place that reduce the identified risks. Required.

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule
_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.title: Carry out an accurate and thorough risk analysis
requirement.description: The risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of all electronic health information the hospital holds are assessed. Required.
requirement.evidence_expected: Risk analysis covering every system that holds health information; date and scope

_labels.version: FV-0002 · HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirement.description: Under the 2026 changes, the notice explains how to exercise rights and that patients may discuss the notice with a named contact, and written acknowledgment of receipt is no longer required.

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.description: Under the 2026 changes, an estimated fee schedule for copies provided under the right of access and under an authorization is posted on the website.
requirement.guidance: From the HIPAA Privacy Rule changes issued November 16, 2026. They take effect 60 days after Federal Register publication, with compliance required 180 days later. The date shown is a placeholder: replace it once the rule is published.

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.description: Under the 2026 changes, access is given as soon as practicable and within 15 calendar days, with one extension of up to 30 days.
requirement.guidance: From the HIPAA Privacy Rule changes issued November 16, 2026. They take effect 60 days after Federal Register publication, with compliance required 180 days later. The date shown is a placeholder: replace it once the rule is published.

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Keep required documentation for six years
requirement.description: Policies, notices, authorizations, complaints and other required records are retained for six years from creation or last effective date.
requirement.evidence_expected: Retention schedule; sample of retained records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Keep privacy policies and procedures current
requirement.description: Written policies and procedures implement the rule and are changed when the law or the hospital's practices change.

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Apply sanctions to workforce members who break privacy policies
requirement.description: Appropriate sanctions are applied and documented when a workforce member fails to follow privacy policies.

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Provide a process for privacy complaints
requirement.description: Patients can complain about privacy practices, and each complaint and its outcome is documented.

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Protect health information with administrative, technical and physical safeguards
requirement.description: Appropriate safeguards protect health information in every form, including paper and spoken, from improper use or disclosure.
requirement.evidence_expected: Safeguards for paper records, conversations and screens; walk-through notes

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Train the workforce on privacy policies
requirement.description: Every workforce member is trained on the privacy policies that apply to their job, on joining and when the policies change.

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Name a privacy official and a contact for complaints
requirement.description: A privacy official is responsible for privacy policies, and a contact person or office receives complaints and gives information about the notice.

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.title: Provide an accounting of disclosures on request
requirement.description: On request, a patient is given a list of certain disclosures made in the previous six years, within 60 days.
requirement.evidence_expected: Disclosure log; accounting requests and responses

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule
_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

requirement.evidence_expected: Amendment requests with outcome and reason

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

_labels.version: FV-0001 · HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

items.report:
AUDIT REPORT (DRAFT): Integrated HIPAA and ISO 27001 internal audit 2026
Project HSP-0001/2026/AUD-0002 · Lakeshore Regional Medical Center · Integrated HIPAA and ISO 27001

1. Objectives
Assess compliance with the HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules, and conformity of the ISMS with ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

2. Scope and exclusions
All clinical and support departments at the main campus, the central laboratory and the hospital data center.
Exclusions: Millcreek outpatient clinic (next cycle); research registry.

3. Audit criteria
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems (2022)
- Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient Records (42 CFR Part 2 (2024 final rule))
- HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400 to 164.414)
- HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)
- HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E)

4. Work performed
180 audit tests planned: 68 passed, 8 failed, 0 not applicable, 104 not yet tested. 48 have been reviewed and approved.

5. Findings
3 minor nonconformity, 1 observation, 3 major nonconformity.
5.1 FND-0007 [Minor nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.8.8: Vulnerability management review: test failed
    9 critical findings older than 30 days, 3 on internet-facing systems.
5.2 FND-0006 [Observation] ISO 27001 A.7.7: A.7.7 Clear desk and clear screen: test failed
    At 6 of 10 nursing stations visited, screens were unlocked and unattended.
5.3 FND-0005 [Minor nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.8.22: A.8.22 Segregation of networks: test failed
    MRI and CT consoles sit on the same network segment as general workstations.
5.4 FND-0004 [Major nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.5.18: A.5.18 Access rights: test failed
    Quarterly access review covered the EHR only. 4 of 25 sampled leavers still had active LIS or PACS accounts.
5.5 FND-0003 [Major nonconformity] HIPAA Privacy 164.502(b): 164.502(b) Limit uses, disclosures and requests to the minimum necessary: test failed
    Each teleradiology request sends the patient's full imaging history. No minimum necessary protocol exists for this routine disclosure.
5.6 FND-0002 [Minor nonconformity] HIPAA Security 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D): 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) Review records of information system activity regularly: test failed
    Access logs of the EHR are kept for 90 days and LIS and PACS logs for 30 days. No scheduled review of any of them was evidenced.
5.7 FND-0001 [Major nonconformity] HIPAA Privacy 164.504(e): 164.504(e) Have a business associate agreement with each vendor that handles health information: test failed
    Two business associates (teleradiology and text messaging vendor) process patient data without a contract containing business associate terms.

6. Conclusion
To be written by the lead auditor. This draft states what the records show and gives no audit opinion.

glossary.full: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
glossary.text: The federal law that protects health information. Its Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules apply to hospitals and to the vendors that handle their data.
Health information that can be tied to a person and is held by a hospital, a health plan or their vendors. HIPAA limits how it is used and shared; ePHI is the electronic form.
An organization HIPAA applies to directly: a health care provider that bills electronically, a health plan or a clearinghouse. A hospital is a covered entity.
A vendor that creates, receives, keeps or sends protected health information for the hospital. It needs a signed agreement before it starts and must report breaches to the hospital.
The contract HIPAA requires with each business associate. It sets permitted uses, safeguards, breach reporting and what happens to the data at the end.
The document that tells patients how the hospital uses their health information and what rights they have. HIPAA sets its content, and it must be given, posted and on the website.
A patient's signed permission for a use or disclosure that HIPAA does not otherwise allow, such as marketing. The patient can revoke it in writing at any time.

glossary.full: Treatment, Payment and Health Care Operations
glossary.text: The three everyday purposes for which HIPAA lets a hospital use and share health information without a signed authorization.
The rule that only the health information needed for the purpose is used, shared or asked for. It does not apply to disclosures for treatment.
A patient's right to see and get a copy of their records. The limit is 30 days today and becomes 15 calendar days when the Privacy Rule changes issued in November 2026 take effect.

An impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured protected health information. It is presumed reportable unless a four-factor risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised.
The four-factor review HIPAA requires after an impermissible disclosure: what information, who got it, whether it was actually viewed, and how far the risk was reduced.
The accurate and thorough assessment of risks to electronic health information that the Security Rule requires. Federal enforcement cites a missing or partial one more often than any other gap.

glossary.full: Department of Health and Human Services
glossary.text: The federal department that issues and enforces the HIPAA rules. Breaches are reported to it.
The part of HHS that investigates HIPAA complaints and breaches and can impose penalties. Patients can complain to it directly.
The federal agency that pays hospitals under Medicare and sets the Conditions of Participation, the emergency care rules and the price transparency rules.
The federal standards a hospital must meet to be paid by Medicare and Medicaid. They cover patient rights, medical records, quality and emergency readiness, among others.

glossary.full: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
glossary.text: The federal law that requires a hospital emergency department to screen and stabilize anyone who comes for care, whatever their ability to pay.
The federal rule that gives extra protection to substance use disorder treatment records. It applies only to federally assisted programs and the records they share.
A practice that is likely to interfere with access to, exchange or use of electronic health information. Federal rules prohibit it unless a listed exception applies.
The published collection of federal agency rules. A reference such as 45 CFR 164.312 means title 45, part 164, section 312.
A requirement whose compliance date has not arrived yet. It is shown as readiness and kept out of the in-force score.
A voluntary federal framework that organizes security work into six functions: govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover.
Twenty voluntary goals HHS published for health care in 2024: ten essential and ten enhanced. They point at the practices that stop the most common attacks.
The body that publishes international standards. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 sets the requirements for an information security management system.
The policies, roles, risk process and controls an organization uses to manage information security in a planned way. ISO/IEC 27001 defines what it must contain.
The document that lists every Annex A control, says whether the hospital needs it and why, and records its implementation status. Each approved version is kept.

The list of 93 reference controls at the back of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, in four themes: organizational, people, physical and technological. Every one must be accounted for in the Statement of Applicability.
The person accountable for information security. In many hospitals the IT head holds this role.
Signing in with a second proof, such as a code from a phone app, as well as a password. Here it is called two-step sign-in.
Giving access according to a person's role rather than person by person. In this product a role sets what each module allows, narrowed further by hospital, department and audit assignment.
Signing in once through the organization's identity system instead of a separate password for each application.
The longest a system may be down after a failure before the harm is unacceptable. The requirements document sets an initial target of 4 hours for this product.
The most data, measured in time, that may be lost in a failure. The requirements document sets an initial target of 1 hour for this product.
A system that collects security logs from many sources and raises alerts. Incidents can be fed from it.
The systems that create user identities and control what each can reach. It supplies information for access reviews.
Reading the words in a scanned page or photograph so they can be searched. It is used on evidence documents.
The level of a risk before any controls are taken into account, scored as likelihood multiplied by impact on scales of 1 to 5.
The level of a risk that remains after controls. A low residual score does not accept the risk: acceptance needs approval by an authorized person.
The decision about what to do with a risk: modify it with controls, retain it, avoid it or share it. Treatment actions are tracked to completion.
The combined practice of directing an organization, managing what could go wrong, and proving that laws and standards are followed.
The action taken to fix a problem that was found and to stop it happening again. Closure needs implementation evidence and an effectiveness check by someone other than the owner or implementer.
A requirement that is not met. A major nonconformity is a failure that undermines the system or the requirement as a whole; a minor one is a lapse that does not.
Something the auditor noticed that is not a nonconformity today but could become one, or the record of what was found in a test.
The recorded result of comparing what the auditor saw with the audit criterion. A finding keeps the link to the test it came from.
The requirement an audit test is judged against, such as a section of the HIPAA rules or an ISO clause, in a specific framework version.
The auditor's record of a test: what was examined, the sample, the result and the reviewer. Only auditors assigned to the audit can see them.
A measure the hospital operates to meet a requirement or reduce a risk. One control can be mapped to several requirements across frameworks, so its evidence is collected once.
A document or record that shows a control operates. Uploading it proves nothing until a reviewer who did not submit it has accepted it.
Whether a requirement applies to a particular hospital. A not-applicable decision needs a written justification and approval, and can be reassessed when operations or the law change.
Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant.
A measure of how well something is working. Each one here shows its calculation rule on hover.
Software provided over the internet for a subscription rather than installed by each customer.
A consultant running assessments and audits for several hospitals from one account. Each consultant sees only the hospitals assigned to them.
One customer organization on a shared installation. Each tenant's data is kept apart from every other tenant's.
The system that holds patients' clinical records and through which most care is ordered and documented.
The messages a hospital system sends when a patient is admitted, moved or discharged. Other systems use them to stay in step.
The number a hospital gives each patient. Records in this product refer to people by reference numbers, not names.
A network through which hospitals and other providers share patient records electronically.
The system that holds employee records. It can supply joiner and leaver dates for access reviews.
The number CMS assigns to a hospital that takes part in Medicare. It identifies the hospital in federal records.
The largest accrediting body for United States hospitals. This product does not issue accreditation; the same controls and evidence can support a survey.
The system that manages laboratory orders, samples and results.
The system that stores and displays radiology images such as X-rays, CT and MRI scans.

glossary.full: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine
glossary.text: The standard format and protocol for medical images. Imaging machines use it to send studies to the PACS.
A family of standards for exchanging clinical and administrative data between health systems.
The modern HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web interfaces.
The finance and purchasing system of record. It can supply vendor and contract information.
A defined way for one system to exchange data with another.
The standard for sending email. Notifications can be emailed when a mail server is configured.
A standard for passing user account information between systems.
The standard used for single sign-on with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Okta.

scores.name: HIPAA compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: HIPAA readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view
combined.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. scores.name: HIPAA compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: HIPAA readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view
combined.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. This combines both frameworks for day-to-day tracking only. It is not a legal compliance determination and not an ISO certification result.

scores.name: HIPAA compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: HIPAA readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view
combined.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. This combines both frameworks for day-to-day tracking only. It is not a legal compliance determination and not an ISO certification result.

coverage.name: Assessment coverage (all HIPAA requirements)
coverage.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

coverage.name: Assessment coverage
coverage.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

on_time.name: Closed within the resolution date
on_time.rule: Closed requests resolved on or before their resolution date, divided by all closed requests.

kpis.name: HIPAA compliance score (requirements in force)

kpis.name: HIPAA readiness (requirements not yet in force)
kpis.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

kpis.name: Assessment coverage (all HIPAA requirements)
kpis.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

on_time.name: Closed within the resolution date

kpis.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
kpis.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

kpis.name: Assessment coverage
kpis.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

kpis.name: Annex A controls implemented
kpis.rule: Controls recorded as implemented in the Statement of Applicability, divided by the controls marked necessary. This is implementation status, not a test of effectiveness.

kpis.name: Statement of Applicability decided
kpis.rule: Annex A controls with an inclusion or exclusion decision, divided by all Annex A controls in the statement.

kpis.name: Controls serving both HIPAA and ISO 27001
kpis.rule: Active controls mapped to at least one HIPAA requirement and at least one ISO 27001 requirement, divided by all active controls.

kpis.name: Controls with accepted evidence
kpis.rule: Active controls with at least one piece of evidence that a reviewer has accepted, divided by all active controls.

kpis.name: Controls operating effectively
kpis.rule: Active controls concluded as operating effectively by a person, after a passed and reviewed test, divided by all active controls.

assignment.title: Patient privacy and HIPAA: the essentials · Denise Rogers

_labels.program: TRN-0001 · Patient privacy and HIPAA: the essentials

program.title: Patient privacy and HIPAA: the essentials
program.description: Starter program. Replace the questions with your own.

questions.q: A patient's relative asks at the nursing station for a copy of the patient's results. What do you do first?
options: Hand them over, they are family
Confirm the patient has agreed or the relative is a personal representative, following the hospital procedure
Ask them to email the doctor

questions.q: Which of these is protected health information?
options: The number of beds on the unit
A patient's medical record number with their diagnosis

questions.q: A patient wants to revoke an authorization to use their story in a newsletter. Who can record it?
options: It is logged as a revocation and acted on by the owner of that activity

questions.q: You sent a discharge summary to the wrong email address. What should you do?
options: Wait and see if anyone notices
Report it at once as an incident
Delete the sent mail and move on
Ask the recipient to ignore it and tell nobody
